title: lore agents gains --target claude|codex; --force runs the marketplace plugin update for the named runtime (rulings 19, 21, 25, 26; Amendment 5)
description: Routed by opum-agent OPAG-421; RE-SCOPED 2026-09-26 by the orchestrator's ruling (option A), binding once recorded as Amendment 5 of opum-doc's docs/adr/distribute-lore-and-quest-agent-skills-through-the-plugin-marketplace.md (read it there on opum-doc origin/main before implementing; Amendments 1-4 at 7831fff). Why: lore agents took only --force and --check (dev df3fecb4), so ruling 25 ('a plugin update runs only for the runtime the user named with --target') could never fire for lore. SHAPE: (1) lore agents gains --target claude|codex, additive: the bare call's published behaviour and every exit code are unchanged. (2) With --target <rt>: bridge regeneration/check is scoped to that runtime (as lore init --claude already is), data.plugin describes that runtime, and --force runs that runtime's plugin update. (3) With no --target: both bridges are checked/regenerated exactly as today, plugin state is reported in data.plugins.<runtime> ONLY (no bare data.plugin; LCLI-592 lands that shape), and no plugin update runs for any runtime. UPDATE (rulings 19, 21, 25, 26(iii); parity with quest-cli QCLI-371's 'quest agents --update-instructions', opum-ai/quest-cli#266, 30a6846): installed + --target names it + --force -> claude: 'claude plugin update opum-lore@opum --scope <deciding scope>'; codex (no per-plugin update): 'codex plugin marketplace upgrade opum' then 'codex plugin add opum-lore@opum', saying in its own output that the Codex upgrade refreshes every opum plugin (ruling 25). Disabled: never enable; report and print the enable command (ruling 21). Not-installed / not-detectable: nothing runs; repo-copy path unchanged. Report update: ran|not-run, updateOk, updateDetail, matching QCLI-371's field names; a failed update keeps exit 0. Long timeout on the Codex upgrade (quest-cli measured >120s). Depends on LCLI-592.

acceptanceCriteria.text: lore agents accepts --target claude|codex: with it, bridge check/regeneration is scoped to that runtime and data.plugin describes that runtime; without it, behaviour and exit codes are unchanged, plugin state appears only in data.plugins.<runtime>, and no bare data.plugin is emitted

With the plugin installed, --target naming the runtime, and --force, lore agents runs the scoped update (claude) or marketplace upgrade plus add (codex, with the all-opum-plugins notice) and reports update/updateOk/updateDetail; a failed update keeps exit 0

A bare lore agents --force (no --target), a disabled plugin, and a not-installed or not-detectable plugin run nothing and print the remedy; the repo-copy path is unchanged when the plugin is absent or undetectable
Tests drive the update path through a stub runtime binary on PATH, never the real claude/codex, and LORE_AGENT_PLUGINS=off runs nothing

docs (cli-surface, cli-contract, lore instructions agents) describe --target and the data.plugin/data.plugins rule; the PR cites Amendment 5 on opum-doc origin/main; bun test and bun run lore check exit 0
